verdicts.claim: Tony Allen 'died 2024'
verdicts.note: Contradicted other dossiers. A live search found no report of his death, and found coverage of his No. 9 jersey retirement in March 2025. Changed to "No. 9 retired March 2025"; his likeness is now framed as licensing, not estate.

verdicts.claim: Penny Hardaway is Memphis Tigers head coach for 2026-27
verdicts.note: Memphis AD Ed Scott retained Hardaway in March 2026 after a 13-19 season, with a contract through 2028. The program is struggling, so Penny-as-halo is softer than the brief implies.

verdicts.claim: Ticer and Hudman still operate Hog & Hominy and Andrew Michael Italian Kitchen
verdicts.note: Search found no closure reports (Hog & Hominy rebuilt after a 2020 fire, and the group is reportedly expanding), but no recent confirmation either. Kept, and queued for a live check.

verdicts.claim: Pyramid was 'home of the Grizzlies' predecessors and Tigers'
verdicts.note: The Grizzlies themselves played there 2001-04. Text fixed.

verdicts.claim: Moneybagz (rapper)
verdicts.note: The name is Moneybagg Yo. Fixed.

verdicts.claim: Twin-arch M bridge named as 'Memphis-Arkansas Bridge and Hernando de Soto Bridge'
verdicts.note: The M-shaped I-40 bridge is the Hernando de Soto only. The Memphis-Arkansas Memorial Bridge is a different crossing. Place renamed.

verdicts.claim: Sun Studio 'Marion Keisker-era signage'
verdicts.note: Unsupported and oddly specific. Replaced with generic vintage signage.

verdicts.claim: Young Dolph 'Makeda's Cookies ties'
verdicts.note: Insensitive and unnecessary, given how he died. Memorial framing kept.

verdicts.claim: 'Whoop that Trick' attributed to Three 6 Mafia era
verdicts.note: It's Al Kapone's song, as the fanbase dossier already said, and an arena victory tradition. Uniform vocabulary now agrees.

verdicts.claim: 'Whoop that Trick / Tear da Club Up' both tied to Three 6 Mafia
verdicts.note: Tear da Club Up is Three 6 Mafia; Whoop That Trick is Al Kapone. The art vocabulary line still groups them, so the editor should split it.

verdicts.claim: Nike era began 2018 (eras: 2001-2018, 2018-present)
verdicts.note: Nike took over the NBA uniform contract in 2017-18. Era boundaries moved to 2017.

verdicts.claim: 2018-19 City Edition 'tied to Memphis music identity'
verdicts.note: No confident basis, so the concept is now marked unverified. Whether a 2017-18 City Edition exists is queued.

verdicts.claim: Zach Randolph 'statue honoree'
verdicts.note: Not confident a statue exists. Replaced with the confirmed No. 50 retirement.

verdicts.claim: Believe Memphis was the slogan of the 2013 West finals run
verdicts.note: The slogan began with the 2011 upset run. Text now covers 2011 through 2013.

verdicts.claim: 'Zeus' as a Zach Randolph fan nickname
verdicts.note: No known basis; likely hallucination.

verdicts.claim: Memphis rap is 'the global default sound for phonk'
verdicts.note: Overclaim. Softened to core source sound.

verdicts.claim: Beale Street blue as '#12274A Grizzlies navy'
verdicts.note: Contradicted the official Midnight Blue #12173F, so recast as a designer-derived night navy. The strategy's Tape Deck "Night navy #12274A" is a designer color and fine.

verdicts.claim: Liberty Bowl Memorial Stadium (also in rhythm, culture)
verdicts.note: Renamed Simmons Bank Liberty Stadium in 2022. Names updated in food, culture and rhythm.

verdicts.claim: Grizzlies 'Sunrise Yellow' (also art, culture, fanbase, rhythm, retail-behavior)
verdicts.note: The official color name is Sunset Yellow (#F5B112). Fixed across dossiers, including art and culture, which labeled #F5B112 as "Stax" or "Sun Studio" yellow.

verdicts.claim: Foot Locker is an independent chain door
verdicts.note: Foot Locker was acquired by Dick's Sporting Goods in 2025 (from memory). Added to the verification queue.

verdicts.claim: 'Shelby County Schools' calendar
verdicts.note: The district is Memphis-Shelby County Schools. Verify line fixed.

verdicts.claim: Beale Street Blue #5D76A9, Midnight Blue #12173F, Sunset Yellow #F5B112, Smoke Blue #707271
verdicts.note: Matches the team's long-standing published palette.

verdicts.claim: Larry Finch led Memphis State to the 1973 title game. Randolph, Gasol and Allen are the Grit and Grind core, and Randolph's No. 50 is retired

verdicts.claim: Royal Studios, Stax Museum, Sun Studio, Hi-Tone, Goner Records, WYXR, Overton Park Shell operate

verdicts.note: Site and format shifted around the Tom Lee Park renovations. Confirm 2027 dates and venue before the Pit Team timing relies on it.

verdicts.claim: Africa in April is a running Memphis festival
verdicts.note: Long-running, but unconfirmed for 2026-27.

verdicts.note: The festival has had cancellations or pauses, so timing is softened. Don't cite it as a 2026 venue without confirmation.

verdicts.claim: Brooks Museum move downtown; Final Friday trolley tours in South Main
verdicts.note: Brooks relocation timing and Final Friday program status are unconfirmed.

verdicts.claim: Four Way, Cozy Corner, Payne's, Gus's, Interstate, Central BBQ open at listed locations; Central BBQ stand inside arena

verdicts.note: Plausible, but unconfirmed for 2027. The September events (Gonerfest, Cooper-Young, Southern Heritage Classic) have passed for 2026.

verdicts.claim: Nike has no owned door (no factory store) in the Memphis metro
verdicts.note: A core strategic premise. Confirm whether any Nike factory or community store exists.

verdicts.note: The strategy names them as pop-up and partner doors. Confirm each before outreach.

verdicts.claim: Tennessee late-July clothing tax holiday under $100 continues; Memphis sales tax about 9.75%
verdicts.note: The back-to-school pack and price statements depend on it. Confirm the 2027 holiday and local rate.

verdicts.claim: Memphis Hustle at Landers Center, the Team Penny circuit, and Gaston Community Center active
verdicts.note: Believed true through 2025-26, but oddly specific. Confirm or drop.

verdicts.claim: Uniform brief steers away from 'music-heritage themes past Memphis City Editions have used'
verdicts.note: The premise rests on unverified City Edition histories. The editor should hedge until the 2026-27 revival and prior concepts are confirmed.

verdicts.claim: Risk and verify entries cite a dossier conflict over Tony Allen's status
verdicts.note: Conflict resolved: Allen is not reported dead (No. 9 retired March 2025) and rhythm is fixed. The editor should delete the conflict wording.

verdicts.claim: Tape Deck play places Southern Heritage Classic, Cooper-Young Festival and Gonerfest in 'mid-to-late September'
verdicts.note: 2026 editions have passed, so the plan is for September 2027, with dates unconfirmed. The editor should say next September and confirm.

verdicts.claim: JJJ to Utah, Morant to Portland, Boozer No. 3, 25-57, Iisalo, Cup West Group B, MLK vs Houston, no opening-night or Christmas game
verdicts.note: All match the verified CURRENT FACTS.

summary: Checked the 11 dossiers and the brief against CURRENT FACTS and three live searches. Team facts hold up everywhere, and Penny Hardaway's 2026-27 return is confirmed. The real errors were smaller. Tony Allen was wrongly reported dead (his No. 9 was retired in March 2025). Others: the Pyramid and bridge descriptions, Moneybagg Yo's name, the Nike-era start, the yellow's name (Sunset, not Sunrise), the stadium rename, a Zeus nickname and an unsupported Keisker detail. Open risk is local operating status and the unverified City Edition history. The strategy needs three edits: cut the Allen conflict wording, hedge the music-theme premise, and mark the September festival plays as 2027.
